title: Cap. VI Arg. 3 close: good pleasure vs foresight faith — Rom. 4:16 not parallel for election
pass_a_gloss: Lastly the Remonstrants say that we err when we oppose good pleasure or the mere grace of God and foresighted faith in this business of predestination; as if we were saying to elect from mere grace and good pleasure, and from foresighted faith; whereas the Apostle from the fact that the inheritance is of faith concludes that it is of grace, Rom. 4:16. But there is not a like reason of obtaining predestination or election, and of entering upon the inheritance of the heavenly kingdom. In the business of election, to be of faith and to be of mere grace are ἐναντία (contraries), because this faith is presupposed to election, which is unto the first grace, and the fountain of all saving grace. But in the matter of entering upon eternal life they are not ἐναντία, because this faith is the gift of pure grace; and so the reward of life which is rendered to the believer is grace for grace. To this is added that since God has proposed to the human race a double way of obtaining salvation, one through the works of the Law, Do this, and you shall live; another through faith in the Mediator, Believe, and you shall be saved, it is rightly said that what is given from faith is given from grace; as what is given from the Law is from works. For it was the singular benefit of Gospel grace, the legal covenant being relaxed, to save sinners through faith. But on the other side the Remonstrants will never prove that God ordained a double mode of predestining men: one according to works, and another according to faith. If therefore some men were elected from an act of believing performed by them, and others were not elected because that same act was omitted, this discrimination would arise not from some special pact or act of Divine grace, but from discriminated acts of human wills. For Peter's predestination would be not from special grace of God, but from Peter's special work: because believing is here considered as a work of choice prevented by grace, opposite to the contrary act of disbelieving; not as a work of some Gospel covenant opposite to the Legal covenant, since concerning predestination such covenants do not exist on either side.
pass_b_english: Lastly Remonstrants say we err in opposing good pleasure (mere grace) to foresighted faith — as if electing from mere grace and from foresighted faith were rivals — since Paul, from inheritance being of faith, concludes it is of grace (Rom. 4:16). The cases are not alike. In election, of faith and of mere grace are ἐναντία: that faith is presupposed to election unto first grace, the spring of all saving grace. In entering eternal life they are not contraries: that faith is pure grace gift, so the life-reward rendered to the believer is grace for grace. God set the race a double path to salvation — Law: Do this and live; Mediator: Believe and be saved — so what comes by faith is rightly called grace, as what comes by Law is from works. Gospel grace singular gift, the legal covenant relaxed, is to save sinners by faith. Remonstrants will never prove God ordained a double mode of predestining — one by works, one by faith. If some were elected for a believing act they performed, and others passed over for omitting it, the split would come not from a special pact of divine grace but from differing human wills. Peter's predestination would then be from Peter's special work, not God's special grace: believing here counts as a work of grace-prevented choice against disbelieving — not as a Gospel-covenant work against the Legal, since no such covenants exist for predestination either way.
source_text: Postremo dicunt Remonstrantes, nos errare, quando beneplacitum sive meram Dei gratiam et fidem praevisam in hoc negotio praedestinationis opponimus; quasi essent dicamus ex mera gratia et beneplacito, atque ex praevisa fide eligere; cum Apostolus ex eo quod haereditas sit ex fide, concludat eam esse ex gratia, Rom. iv. 16. Sed non est par ratio praedestinationis sive electionis obtinendae, et haereditatis regni caelestis adeundae. In negotio electionis esse ex fide, et esse ex mera gratia sunt ἐναντία, quia haec fides praesupponitur electioni, quae est ad primam gratiam, et scaturigo omnis gratiae salutiferae. At in causa adeundae vitae aeternae non sunt ἐναντία, quia haec fides est purae gratiae donum; et sic vitae praemium quod credenti redditur, est gratia pro gratia. Huc accedit, quod cum Deus humano generi proposuerit duplicem viam consequendae salutis, unam per opera Legis, Hoc fac, et vives; aliam per fidem Mediatoris, Crede, et salvus eris, recte dicitur ex gratia dari, quod datur ex fide; sicut ex operibus, quod datur ex Lege. Fuit enim gratiae Evangelicae singulare beneficium, relaxato foedere legali, salvare peccatores per fidem. At vero ex altera parte nunquam probabunt Remonstrantes Deum ordinasse duplicem modum praedestinandi homines: unum secundum opera, et alium secundum fidem. Si ergo quidam homines ex actu credendi ab illis praestito eligerentur, alii ob eundem actum omissum non eligerentur, discrimen hoc oriretur non ex speciali aliquo pacto aut actu gratiae Divinae, sed ex discriminatis actibus voluntatum humanarum. Esset enim praedestinatio Petri non ex speciali gratia Dei, sed ex speciali opere Petri: quia credere hic consideratur ut opus arbitrii per gratiam praeventi, oppositum contrario actui discredendi; non ut opus pacti alicujus Evangelici, oppositum pacto Legali, cum de praedestinatione talia pacta non exstent in utramvis partem.
